collection.name: Collocations & Idioms
collection.description: English collocations and idioms grouped for IELTS study, with Vietnamese meanings for intermediate learners.

meta.note: First 200 entries are fully Claude-authored (part of speech, IPA, definition, synonyms, collocations, examples, IELTS difficulty band; no external LLM). The remaining entries are seeded (word + Vietnamese meaning) from an imported vocabulary source and await a later enrichment batch. Fields map onto lib/types.ts.

words.vi_meaning: gia đình ruột thịt (gồm cha, mẹ, vợ/chồng và anh chị em ruột)
words.definition_en: The people you are most closely related to, such as your parents, brothers and sisters, spouse and children.
collocations: a member of the immediate family
words.example_simple: Only my immediate family came to the small wedding.
words.example_complex: Hospital policy allows visits from the patient's immediate family, so distant cousins were asked to wait outside.
words.false_friend_note: "Immediate" here means closest in relationship, not "immediately/right away".

words.vi_meaning: đại gia đình (gồm cả ông bà, cô, dì, chú, bác, cậu, mợ...)
words.definition_en: A family group that includes not only parents and children but also grandparents, aunts, uncles and cousins.
words.example_simple: My extended family meets every year for Tết.
words.example_complex: In many rural areas, several generations of an extended family still live together under one roof.

words.vi_meaning: sơ đồ gia phả (biểu đồ thể hiện các thế hệ và mối quan hệ trong gia đình)
words.definition_en: A diagram that shows the members of a family over several generations and how they are related.
collocations: a branch of the family tree
words.example_simple: We drew a family tree for our history homework.
words.example_complex: Researching old records, she traced her family tree back more than two hundred years.

words.definition_en: A member of your family who is not closely related to you, such as a second cousin.
collocations: a distant relative on my mother's side
words.example_simple: A distant relative I had never met came to the funeral.
words.example_complex: The estate was eventually left to a distant relative whom the family had lost touch with decades earlier.
words.false_friend_note: "Distant" refers to closeness of relationship, not physical distance.

words.vi_meaning: gia đình đầm ấm, yêu thương nhau
words.definition_en: A family whose members care deeply about and show affection to one another.
collocations: grow up in a loving family
words.example_simple: She grew up in a loving family.
words.example_complex: Despite their modest means, the children thrived in a loving family that put togetherness above everything else.

words.vi_meaning: gia đình không êm ấm, có nhiều mâu thuẫn và trục trặc
words.definition_en: A family in which there are constant conflicts, poor communication or unhealthy behaviour between members.
words.example_simple: He came from a dysfunctional family and left home young.
words.example_complex: The novel portrays a dysfunctional family whose secrets and resentments slowly tear it apart.

words.vi_meaning: tuổi thơ êm đềm, vô lo vô nghĩ
words.definition_en: A childhood spent happily and without worries or serious problems.
collocations: a carefree childhood in the countryside
words.example_simple: I had a carefree childhood by the sea.
words.example_complex: Looking back, he cherished the carefree childhood he had spent roaming the fields before adult responsibilities set in.
words.false_friend_note: "Carefree" (vô lo) is not the same as "careless" (bất cẩn).

words.vi_meaning: tuổi thơ khó khăn, nhiều bất hạnh
words.definition_en: A childhood marked by problems, unhappiness or difficult experiences.
collocations: the scars of a troubled childhood
words.example_simple: Her troubled childhood made it hard for her to trust people.
words.example_complex: In interviews he spoke openly about a troubled childhood shaped by poverty and his parents' divorce.

words.vi_meaning: cuộc ly hôn cay đắng, đầy xích mích và oán giận
words.definition_en: A divorce full of anger and resentment, in which the couple part on very bad terms.
words.example_simple: They went through a bitter divorce last year.
words.example_complex: Following a bitter divorce, the couple could barely speak to each other even about their children.
words.false_friend_note: The seed "ly thân" means separation; a divorce (ly hôn) legally ends the marriage.

words.vi_meaning: cuộc ly hôn rắc rối, lộn xộn (thường có tranh chấp tài sản, con cái)
words.definition_en: A divorce that is complicated and full of arguments, often over money, property or the children.
collocations: in the middle of a messy divorce
words.example_simple: Their messy divorce dragged on for two years.
words.example_complex: The company's founder was distracted throughout the merger by a messy divorce involving disputed assets.

words.vi_meaning: ly hôn/ly thân trong hòa thuận, cả hai bên đồng thuận, không tranh chấp
words.definition_en: A divorce or separation that both partners agree to, without serious arguments or disputes.
words.example_simple: It was a mutual separation, so there were no arguments.
words.example_complex: The couple issued a joint statement describing their split as a mutual separation reached with respect on both sides.
words.false_friend_note: "Mutual" means shared/agreed by both, not "tương hỗ" in a technical sense here.

words.vi_meaning: gia đình tan vỡ (cha mẹ ly hôn hoặc ly thân)
words.definition_en: A family in which the parents have divorced or separated, so the children no longer live with both of them.
collocations: grow up in a broken home
words.example_simple: He came from a broken home but did well at school.
words.example_complex: Social workers argued that support, not stigma, was what children from a broken home most needed.

words.vi_meaning: mẹ đơn thân (người mẹ nuôi con một mình)
words.definition_en: A woman who raises her child or children on her own, without a partner.
words.example_simple: As a single mother, she works two jobs.
words.example_complex: The scheme offers childcare grants to help single mothers return to full-time work.

words.definition_en: To end a pregnancy deliberately through a medical procedure.
words.example_simple: She decided to have an abortion after talking to her doctor.
words.example_complex: Whether women should be legally able to get an abortion remains a deeply divisive political issue.
words.false_friend_note: "Abortion" is a sensitive term; note it is the noun, and you "have/get" one (not "do").

words.vi_meaning: buổi đoàn tụ/sum họp gia đình
words.definition_en: An occasion when members of a family, especially those who live far apart, come together again.
words.example_simple: We have a family reunion every summer.
words.example_complex: The holiday became an emotional family reunion, with relatives flying in from three different continents.

words.vi_meaning: thỏa thuận/phán quyết phân chia khi ly hôn (tài sản, tiền cấp dưỡng...)
words.definition_en: A legal agreement that decides how money, property and other matters are divided when a couple divorces.
words.example_simple: They finally reached a divorce settlement out of court.
words.example_complex: Under the divorce settlement, she kept the family home while he retained the couple's shares in the business.

words.vi_meaning: quyền nuôi con (quyền chăm sóc và nuôi dưỡng con sau ly hôn)
words.definition_en: The legal right and responsibility to care for and bring up a child, especially after a divorce.
words.example_simple: She was given custody of the children after the divorce.
words.example_complex: The court awarded custody of the children to their mother but guaranteed the father regular weekend visits.
words.false_friend_note: "Custody" here means legal care of a child, not "tạm giam" (police custody).

words.vi_meaning: trao quyền nuôi con chung (cả cha và mẹ cùng chia sẻ quyền nuôi con)
words.definition_en: When a court gives both parents the shared legal right to care for their child after a divorce.
collocations: grant joint custody to both parents
words.example_simple: The judge granted joint custody, so the children live with each parent half the time.
words.example_complex: After mediation, the court decided to grant joint custody, requiring the parents to cooperate closely on the children's schooling.

words.vi_meaning: quyền nuôi con độc quyền (chỉ một mình cha hoặc mẹ có quyền nuôi con)
words.definition_en: When only one parent has the full legal right to care for and make decisions about a child.
collocations: have sole custody of the children
words.example_simple: The mother was given sole custody of her son.
words.example_complex: Citing the father's frequent absences, the court awarded the mother sole custody of both children.
words.false_friend_note: "Sole" (duy nhất) sounds like "soul" (linh hồn) but is unrelated.

words.vi_meaning: giao/trao quyền nuôi con cho một bên (tòa quyết định chỉ một người có quyền nuôi con)
words.definition_en: When a court officially gives one parent alone the full legal right to care for a child.
collocations: award sole custody to the mother
award sole custody of the child
words.example_simple: The court awarded sole custody to the father.
words.example_complex: After hearing evidence of neglect, the judge awarded sole custody to the grandmother rather than either parent.
words.false_friend_note: "Award" here means to grant officially, not a prize (giải thưởng).

words.vi_meaning: trả tiền trợ cấp nuôi con (sau khi ly hôn)
words.definition_en: To regularly give money to help take care of your child, usually after a divorce or separation.
words.example_simple: He pays child support for his two kids every month.
words.example_complex: Under the court agreement, the father is legally required to pay child support until each child turns eighteen.
words.false_friend_note: 'Support' here means financial help, not 'ủng hộ/động viên' emotionally.

words.vi_meaning: giữ mối quan hệ hòa nhã, thân thiện với ai
words.definition_en: To have a friendly relationship with someone and avoid arguments.
collocations: remain on good terms with colleagues
keep on good terms after a breakup
words.example_simple: I still keep on good terms with my old classmates.
words.example_complex: Even after their business partnership ended, the two founders managed to stay on good terms and occasionally advised each other.
words.false_friend_note: 'Terms' here means the state of a relationship, not 'điều khoản' or 'học kỳ'.

words.definition_en: To become pregnant; to begin having a baby growing inside the body.
words.example_simple: She got pregnant last year and had a baby girl.
words.example_complex: After years of trying, the couple were overjoyed when she finally got pregnant with their first child.

words.vi_meaning: nuôi nấng, nuôi dạy con cái
words.definition_en: To take care of a child and help them grow up, teaching them how to behave.
words.example_simple: It is not easy to raise a child on your own.
words.example_complex: They chose to raise their children in the countryside, believing it offered a healthier and calmer environment.
words.false_friend_note: 'Raise' (nuôi dạy) differs from 'rise' (tự tăng lên); don't confuse the two.

words.definition_en: A child who is legally taken into a family and raised as their own, though not born to them.
words.example_simple: Their adopted child is now a happy teenager.
words.example_complex: The novel explores how an adopted child gradually uncovers the truth about her biological family.
words.false_friend_note: 'Adopt' (nhận nuôi) vs 'adapt' (thích nghi) — very easy to mix up.

words.vi_meaning: đứa con cưng, người được sếp/cấp trên ưu ái nhất
words.definition_en: A man or boy who is treated as a favourite by someone in authority, such as a boss or teacher.
words.example_simple: He's the boss's blue-eyed boy, so he never gets into trouble.
words.example_complex: Once considered the chairman's blue-eyed boy, the young executive lost his privileged status after the failed merger.
words.false_friend_note: It has nothing to do with eye colour; it means a favoured person (often slightly critical).

words.vi_meaning: chung tay, hợp sức, cùng hợp tác
words.definition_en: To work together with others to achieve a shared goal.
words.example_simple: Let's join hands to clean up the beach.
words.example_complex: The two governments agreed to join hands in tackling climate change across the region.
words.false_friend_note: Figurative 'cùng hợp tác'; only sometimes literal (nắm tay nhau).

words.definition_en: To check that something is true or that something will happen as planned.
words.example_simple: Make sure you lock the door before you leave.
words.example_complex: The manager double-checked the figures to make sure that no errors would appear in the final report.

words.vi_meaning: vội vã, đang gấp, đang cần nhanh
words.definition_en: To need to do something quickly because you do not have much time.
collocations: no need to be in a hurry
words.example_simple: Sorry, I can't talk now — I'm in a hurry.
words.example_complex: She spoke quickly and kept glancing at the clock, clearly in a hurry to catch the last train.

words.definition_en: To be fully prepared for something that is about to happen.
words.example_simple: Are you ready to leave?
words.example_complex: After months of training, the athletes felt completely ready to compete on the international stage.

words.vi_meaning: sẵn lòng, sẵn sàng làm gì đó
words.definition_en: To be happy to do something, or not to mind doing it.
words.example_simple: I'm willing to help you with your homework.
words.example_complex: The company said it was willing to negotiate, provided that both sides showed genuine flexibility.
words.false_friend_note: 'Willing' is not the future 'will'; it means 'sẵn lòng', showing attitude, not tense.

words.vi_meaning: giành được một suất, một vị trí (ở trường, đội, cuộc thi)
words.definition_en: To succeed in getting a position or spot, especially at a university, on a team, or in a competition.
collocations: win a place on the team
win a place in the final
words.example_simple: She won a place at a top university.
words.example_complex: After a rigorous selection process, he won a place on the national research programme.

words.vi_meaning: chịu áp lực, bị áp lực
words.definition_en: To feel stressed because people expect a lot from you or you have too much to do.
collocations: be under a lot of pressure
words.example_simple: He is under pressure to finish the project on time.
words.example_complex: The surgeon remained remarkably calm even while under enormous pressure during the emergency operation.

words.word: men build the house and women make it home
words.ipa: /men bɪld ðə haʊs ənd ˈwɪmɪn meɪk ɪt həʊm/
words.vi_meaning: đàn ông xây nhà, đàn bà xây tổ ấm
words.definition_en: A saying meaning that men provide the physical structure while women create the warmth and comfort of a family.
synonyms: a house is not a home without a woman
home is where the heart is
it takes a woman to make a home
words.example_simple: My grandma always says men build the house and women make it home.
words.example_complex: The lecture challenged the old proverb that men build the house and women make it home, arguing that both roles are now shared.
words.false_friend_note: Note 'house' (căn nhà, vật lý) vs 'home' (tổ ấm, tình cảm) — the whole saying depends on this contrast.

words.vi_meaning: dọn bàn ăn, bày biện bàn ăn
words.definition_en: To put plates, knives, forks and other things on a table before a meal.
words.example_simple: Can you lay the table? Dinner is almost ready.
words.example_complex: Before the guests arrived, she carefully laid the table with the family's finest china and silverware.
words.false_friend_note: 'Lay the table' means set it up, not 'đặt cái bàn xuống'.

words.definition_en: To wash clothes, towels and other things that need washing.
collocations: do the laundry once a week
words.example_simple: I need to do the laundry this weekend.
words.example_complex: Between working full-time and raising two children, finding a spare hour just to do the laundry felt impossible.

words.definition_en: To wash the dishes, pots and cutlery after a meal (British English).
collocations: do the washing up after dinner
words.example_simple: You cooked, so I'll do the washing up.
words.example_complex: In their household, whoever did not prepare the meal was expected to do the washing up afterwards.
words.false_friend_note: 'Washing up' (BrE) = rửa bát, not washing yourself or laundry.

words.vi_meaning: gây áp lực lên ai/cái gì
words.definition_en: To try to force or strongly persuade someone to do something, or to strain something.
words.example_simple: Don't put too much pressure on your children to get top marks.
words.example_complex: The rising number of patients continued to put pressure on an already overstretched healthcare system.

words.vi_meaning: làm việc nhà, làm công việc gia đình
words.definition_en: To do the regular jobs that need doing around the home, such as cleaning and tidying.
words.example_simple: We share the household chores in my family.
words.example_complex: Studies suggest that couples who divide the household chores fairly tend to report higher relationship satisfaction.
words.false_friend_note: 'Chores' means routine tasks (việc vặt), not a single big job.

words.vi_meaning: đi mua thực phẩm, đi chợ mua đồ ăn
words.definition_en: To buy food and other things you use every day at a shop or supermarket.
collocations: go out to shop for groceries
words.example_simple: I shop for groceries every Saturday morning.
words.example_complex: During the lockdown, many families began to shop for groceries online rather than visiting crowded supermarkets.
words.false_friend_note: 'Groceries' = thực phẩm/đồ tạp hóa, not 'grocer' (người bán hàng).

words.vi_meaning: quán xuyến việc nhà, lo liệu công việc nhà
words.definition_en: to deal with and take care of the regular jobs around the house
words.example_simple: My brother and I take turns to handle the chores.
words.example_complex: Now that both parents work full-time, they share the responsibility of handling the chores so no one feels overwhelmed.

words.definition_en: the money a family earns, spends and saves
words.example_simple: My mother manages the household finances very carefully.
words.example_complex: With prices rising so quickly, keeping the household finances under control has become a real challenge for many families.

words.vi_meaning: người nội trợ, người quán xuyến việc nhà
words.definition_en: a person who manages a home and family, especially instead of working outside
words.example_simple: She is a full-time homemaker and looks after three children.
words.example_complex: After the birth of their second child, he chose to become a homemaker while his wife returned to her career.
words.false_friend_note: 'Homemaker' is a neutral, modern term; unlike 'housewife' it can refer to a man or a woman.

words.vi_meaning: thay phiên nhau làm gì, luân phiên làm việc gì
words.definition_en: to do something one after another rather than all at the same time
words.example_simple: We take turns doing the washing-up.
words.example_complex: On the long road trip, the three of us took turns driving so that no one got too tired.

words.vi_meaning: trách nhiệm/công việc nhà, việc vặt trong gia đình
words.definition_en: the regular jobs that must be done to run a home, such as cleaning and cooking
words.example_simple: Everyone in the family helps with the household chores.
words.example_complex: Dividing the household duties fairly between partners can prevent a lot of arguments at home.

words.definition_en: to get money by working or doing business
words.example_simple: He works two jobs to make money for his family.
words.example_complex: Many students look for part-time work so they can earn money while still focusing on their studies.
words.false_friend_note: In English you usually 'earn' or 'make' money, not 'win' money (except in games or the lottery).

words.word: East or West, home is best
words.vi_meaning: ta về ta tắm ao ta; không đâu tốt bằng nhà mình
words.definition_en: no matter where you go, your own home is the best place to be
synonyms: home is where the heart is
collocations: as the saying goes, East or West, home is best
believe East or West, home is best
words.example_simple: After travelling for a month, I was happy to be back — East or West, home is best.
words.example_complex: The hotels were luxurious and the sights were amazing, but as we unlocked our own front door I remembered that East or West, home is best.

words.vi_meaning: người quen sơ, người mà bạn không biết rõ lắm
words.definition_en: people you know slightly but are not close friends with
words.example_simple: We are just casual acquaintances, not close friends.
words.example_complex: Although they had met several times at conferences, they remained casual acquaintances who rarely spoke outside of work.
words.false_friend_note: 'Acquaintance' is not the same as a close friend; it means someone you know only a little.

words.vi_meaning: yêu từ cái nhìn đầu tiên; tiếng sét ái tình
words.definition_en: the experience of falling in love with someone the moment you first see them
collocations: believe in love at first sight
it was love at first sight
fall in love at first sight
words.example_simple: For them, it was love at first sight.
words.example_complex: She had never believed in love at first sight until she met him across a crowded room and forgot everything else.

words.vi_meaning: bạn tâm giao; người bạn đời tri kỷ
words.definition_en: a person who is perfectly suited to another, especially in a romantic relationship
words.example_simple: She feels her husband is her soulmate.
words.example_complex: After years of failed relationships, he finally met someone he considered his true soulmate, someone who understood him completely.

words.vi_meaning: cặp trời sinh, đôi lứa xứng đôi, đẹp đôi
words.definition_en: a couple or combination that is perfectly suited to each other
collocations: seem like a match made in heaven
truly a match made in heaven
words.example_simple: They are a match made in heaven.
words.example_complex: With her calm nature and his boundless energy, everyone agreed they were a match made in heaven.

words.definition_en: love that one person feels for another who does not feel the same way
words.example_simple: He suffered from unrequited love for his classmate.
words.example_complex: Much of the poet's early work explores the quiet pain of unrequited love and the hope that one day it might be returned.

words.vi_meaning: ràng buộc, cam kết, giao ước gắn bó
words.definition_en: to promise firmly to do something or to stay loyal to someone
words.example_simple: They decided to make a commitment to each other.
words.example_complex: Before moving in together, the couple sat down and made a real commitment to build a future side by side.

words.vi_meaning: ngoại tình, có quan hệ ngoài luồng
words.definition_en: to have a secret romantic or sexual relationship while married or in a relationship
words.example_simple: She found out that her husband was having an affair.
words.example_complex: The novel follows a respected businessman whose life falls apart after his wife discovers he has been having an affair for years.
words.false_friend_note: In this sense 'affair' means an illicit relationship, not just a general 'matter' or 'event'.

words.vi_meaning: lừa dối ai (trong tình cảm), phản bội bạn đời
words.definition_en: to be unfaithful to your partner by having a relationship with someone else
words.example_simple: He cheated on his girlfriend and she left him.
words.example_complex: When she realised he had been cheating on her the whole time, she packed her bags and never looked back.
words.false_friend_note: 'Cheat on someone' means to be romantically unfaithful; 'cheat in an exam' is a different meaning.

words.vi_meaning: có điểm chung, có điểm giống nhau
words.definition_en: to share interests, features or qualities with another person
words.example_simple: We have a lot in common — we both love music.
words.example_complex: Although they came from very different backgrounds, they soon discovered they had a great deal in common.

words.vi_meaning: quen biết nhau đã lâu, có mối quan hệ từ nhiều năm trước
words.definition_en: to have known each other for a long time
words.example_simple: Tom and I go back years — we met at primary school.
words.example_complex: The two politicians may argue in public, but privately they go back years and still trust each other.

words.vi_meaning: mối quan hệ lúc yêu lúc chia tay, tình cảm lúc hợp lúc tan
words.definition_en: a romantic relationship that repeatedly ends and starts again
words.example_simple: They have been in an on-off relationship for years.
words.example_complex: Their on-off relationship confused all their friends, who could never tell whether the couple were together or broken up that week.

words.vi_meaning: tán tỉnh ai, thể hiện sự thích thú/muốn hẹn hò với ai
words.definition_en: to show someone in a fairly obvious way that you are romantically or sexually attracted to them
collocations: hit on her at the party
words.example_simple: A guy tried to hit on her at the bar.
words.example_complex: He felt embarrassed when he realised he had been hitting on someone who was already married.
words.false_friend_note: 'Hit on someone' means to flirt with them, not to physically strike them.

words.vi_meaning: mời ai đó đi chơi, rủ ai đi hẹn hò
words.definition_en: to invite someone to go on a date with you
collocations: too shy to ask someone out
words.example_simple: He was too nervous to ask her out.
words.example_complex: After weeks of hesitation, he finally worked up the courage to ask his coworker out for dinner.

words.vi_meaning: hợp nhau ngay từ lần đầu gặp; nhanh chóng thân thiết với ai đó
words.definition_en: to like someone and become friendly with them as soon as you meet
words.example_simple: We hit it off the moment we met at the party.
words.example_complex: Although they came from very different backgrounds, the two colleagues hit it off instantly and soon became close friends.

words.vi_meaning: dần dần xa cách nhau; từ từ tách rời khỏi nhau
words.definition_en: to slowly become less close or friendly with someone over time
words.example_simple: After school, my best friend and I slowly drifted apart.
words.example_complex: As their careers pulled them to different cities, the once-inseparable siblings gradually drifted apart.

words.vi_meaning: yêu ai đó say đắm, mê mệt; yêu tít thò lò
words.definition_en: completely and deeply in love with someone
collocations: be head over heels in love
words.example_simple: He is head over heels in love with his new girlfriend.
words.example_complex: Within weeks of their first date, she had fallen head over heels in love and could think of nothing else.

words.vi_meaning: hôn hít, âu yếm ai đó một cách nhiệt tình
words.definition_en: to kiss and touch someone in a sexual way (informal)
words.example_simple: They were making out on the sofa when I walked in.
words.example_complex: The teenagers snuck off to make out behind the gym, hoping no one would notice they were gone.
words.false_friend_note: 'Make out' can also mean 'to manage/cope' or 'to see with difficulty', so context decides the meaning.

words.vi_meaning: thầm thích, phải lòng ai đó (thường ngắn hạn)
words.definition_en: to feel a strong but usually temporary romantic attraction to someone
words.example_simple: I had a crush on my English teacher when I was fifteen.
words.example_complex: She realised she had developed a crush on her coworker only when she started dressing up for the office.

words.vi_meaning: có sự ăn ý, hòa hợp, có 'phản ứng hóa học' với ai đó
words.definition_en: to have a strong natural connection or attraction with someone
words.example_simple: The two actors clearly have chemistry with each other.
words.example_complex: Despite rehearsing for weeks, the leads never quite had the chemistry the director was looking for on screen.
words.false_friend_note: Here 'chemistry' means personal connection, not the school subject.

words.vi_meaning: ngỏ lời cầu hôn; hỏi cưới ai đó
words.definition_en: to ask someone to marry you
words.example_simple: He popped the question on her birthday.
words.example_complex: After dating for five years, he finally popped the question during a surprise trip to Paris.

words.vi_meaning: kết hôn; nên duyên vợ chồng
words.definition_en: to get married
words.example_simple: They tied the knot last June.
words.example_complex: After a long engagement, the couple finally tied the knot in a small ceremony surrounded by family.

words.vi_meaning: (mối quan hệ) đang gặp trục trặc, sắp tan vỡ
words.definition_en: (of a relationship or situation) experiencing serious problems and likely to fail
words.example_simple: Their marriage has been on the rocks for months.
words.example_complex: Rumours that the star couple's relationship was on the rocks intensified after they were seen arguing in public.
words.false_friend_note: 'On the rocks' can also mean a drink served over ice cubes, e.g. 'whisky on the rocks'.

words.vi_meaning: làm lành, giảng hòa sau khi cãi nhau; gương vỡ lại lành
words.definition_en: to become friends again after an argument
collocations: time to kiss and make up
words.example_simple: They had a big fight but soon kissed and made up.
words.example_complex: After weeks of not speaking, the two friends decided it was time to kiss and make up and move on.
words.false_friend_note: Written as two words 'make up' here, not the noun 'makeup' (cosmetics).

words.vi_meaning: tình yêu tuổi mới lớn, tình yêu trẻ con (thường không lâu bền)
words.definition_en: romantic love between young people that is not usually serious or lasting
words.example_simple: Their parents said it was only puppy love.
words.example_complex: What began as harmless puppy love in secondary school unexpectedly blossomed into a lifelong marriage.
words.false_friend_note: Nothing to do with actual puppies; it refers to youthful romantic feelings.

words.vi_meaning: có trái tim sắt đá; lạnh lùng, tàn nhẫn, vô cảm
words.definition_en: to be cruel or unable to show sympathy or emotion
collocations: really have a heart of stone
seem to have a heart of stone
words.example_simple: You must have a heart of stone to ignore a crying child.
words.example_complex: The landlord had a heart of stone, evicting the elderly tenants in the middle of winter without a second thought.

words.vi_meaning: bạn thân, bạn tâm giao, bạn chí cốt
words.definition_en: a friend you know very well and trust completely
words.example_simple: She is one of my closest friends.
words.example_complex: Only a handful of intimate friends knew about the private struggles he had kept hidden for years.
words.false_friend_note: 'Intimate' here means emotionally close, not necessarily romantic or sexual.

words.vi_meaning: người bạn chỉ ở bên khi thuận lợi, rời bỏ bạn lúc khó khăn
words.definition_en: someone who is a friend only when things are going well for you
collocations: turn out to be a fair-weather friend
words.example_simple: When I lost my job, I found out who my fair-weather friends were.
words.example_complex: As soon as his fortune disappeared, the fair-weather friends who had crowded around him vanished overnight.

words.vi_meaning: bạn thời thơ ấu; bạn thời niên thiếu
words.definition_en: a person you have been friends with since you were both children
words.example_simple: We have been childhood friends since we were five.
words.example_complex: By chance she ran into a childhood friend she had not seen for over twenty years at the airport.

words.vi_meaning: không ưa, không ủng hộ ai/cái gì; không phải là bạn của
words.definition_en: to not like or support someone or something
collocations: he is no friend of mine
words.example_simple: He is no friend of the poor.
words.example_complex: The new policy proved that the government was no friend of small businesses struggling to survive.

words.vi_meaning: trường tồn với thời gian; bền vững, vẫn có giá trị qua năm tháng
words.definition_en: to remain good, useful, or popular for a very long time
collocations: truly stand the test of time
friendship stands the test of time
designs that stand the test of time
words.example_simple: Their friendship has stood the test of time.
words.example_complex: Few architectural styles stand the test of time the way classical columns have, remaining admired for thousands of years.

words.vi_meaning: nhanh chóng đứng ra bảo vệ, bênh vực ai đó
words.definition_en: to quickly defend or support someone who is being criticised or attacked
words.example_simple: When they criticised her, her brother sprang to her defence.
words.example_complex: The moment his integrity was questioned in the meeting, several colleagues sprang to his defence.
words.false_friend_note: British spelling 'defence'; American English uses 'defense'.

words.vi_meaning: bị tấn công; bị chỉ trích mạnh mẽ
words.definition_en: to be attacked or strongly criticised
words.example_simple: The minister came under attack for her decision.
words.example_complex: The company's environmental record came under attack from campaigners who demanded an immediate change of policy.

words.word: put some distance between yourself and someone/something
words.vi_meaning: tạo khoảng cách, giữ khoảng cách với ai/cái gì
words.definition_en: to become less involved or connected with someone or something
collocations: put distance between yourself and the past
words.example_simple: She wanted to put some distance between herself and her old life.
words.example_complex: After the scandal, the politician tried to put some distance between himself and the colleagues involved.

words.vi_meaning: tạo dựng, xây đắp một mối quan hệ (bền chặt)
words.definition_en: to build a strong relationship over time, often through effort
words.example_simple: The two companies forged a relationship based on trust.
words.example_complex: Over the years, she forged a strong professional relationship with clients who came to rely on her honest advice.
words.false_friend_note: 'Forge' here means 'to build', not 'to fake/counterfeit' as in 'forge a signature'.

words.word: abuse of trust / a breach of trust
words.ipa: /əˈbjuːs əv trʌst / ə briːtʃ əv trʌst/
words.vi_meaning: sự lạm dụng lòng tin; sự phản bội, bội tín
words.definition_en: the act of breaking the trust that someone has placed in you
words.example_simple: Lying to your friend is an abuse of trust.
words.example_complex: The manager's decision to share confidential files was a clear breach of trust that cost him his job.

words.vi_meaning: cố gắng duy trì, vun đắp cho mối quan hệ với ai đó
words.definition_en: to put in effort so that a relationship succeeds and lasts
collocations: work hard to make the relationship work
words.example_simple: Both people must try to make the relationship work.
words.example_complex: Despite living in different countries, they were determined to make the relationship work through daily calls and regular visits.

words.vi_meaning: làm hòa, hòa giải với ai (sau khi cãi vã)
words.definition_en: to become friendly with someone again after a disagreement
words.example_simple: After years apart, he was reconciled with his brother.
words.example_complex: Following a long and bitter dispute, the two sisters were finally reconciled with each other at their mother's funeral.

words.word: see eye to eye with sb
words.vi_meaning: đồng quan điểm, nhất trí với ai
words.definition_en: to agree with someone completely
collocations: see eye to eye on sth
words.example_simple: My sister and I see eye to eye on most things.
words.example_complex: The two politicians rarely see eye to eye, but on this particular issue they found surprising common ground.
words.false_friend_note: Idiom meaning 'to agree', not a literal act of looking into someone's eyes.

words.word: have a quarrel / row with sb
words.vi_meaning: cãi cọ, cãi nhau to tiếng với ai
words.definition_en: to have an angry argument with someone
words.example_simple: They had a quarrel about money.
words.example_complex: The couple had a terrible row in front of their guests, and the awkward silence that followed ruined the evening.
words.false_friend_note: British 'row' here rhymes with 'now' and means 'argument', not a 'line' or 'to row a boat'.

words.vi_meaning: làm ầm ĩ, làm rối lên, phàn nàn ầm ĩ về chuyện nhỏ
words.definition_en: to complain or become excited about something unimportant
words.example_simple: Don't make a fuss over such a small mistake.
words.example_complex: She hates it when people make a fuss over her birthday, preferring a quiet dinner with close family instead.

words.vi_meaning: phớt lờ, không để tâm, ngừng chú ý lắng nghe
words.definition_en: to stop paying attention to someone or something
words.example_simple: I tune out when the lecture gets boring.
words.example_complex: After hours of the same complaints, he learned to tune out his colleague's endless grumbling and focus on his work.
words.false_friend_note: 'Tune out' (stop listening) is the opposite of 'tune in' (start paying attention).

words.vi_meaning: thú nhận, thổ lộ điều gì với ai
words.definition_en: to admit something, often something bad or secret, to someone
words.example_simple: He confessed his mistake to his boss.
words.example_complex: After weeks of guilt, she finally confessed to her parents that she had failed the exam and hidden the results.

words.vi_meaning: âu yếm, tình tứ, thể hiện tình cảm quá mức (thường nơi công cộng)
words.definition_en: showing love and affection in a very open, sometimes embarrassing way
words.example_simple: The new couple were being all lovey-dovey at the party.
words.example_complex: My friends teased us for being so lovey-dovey in public, but we were just happy to be together after months apart.
words.false_friend_note: Informal and slightly teasing in tone; often implies affection that is a bit excessive.

words.vi_meaning: phá tan bầu không khí ngượng ngùng, mở đầu cuộc trò chuyện với người lạ
words.definition_en: to say or do something to make people feel more relaxed in a new social situation
collocations: break the ice with a joke
words.example_simple: He told a joke to break the ice.
words.example_complex: To break the ice at the training session, the trainer asked everyone to share one unusual fact about themselves.
words.false_friend_note: Idiom about easing social awkwardness, not literally breaking frozen water.

words.word: lend a sympathetic ear to sb
words.vi_meaning: lắng nghe và cảm thông với ai, chia sẻ nỗi lòng của ai
words.definition_en: to listen kindly and with sympathy to someone's problems
synonyms: offer a shoulder to cry on
words.example_simple: She lent a sympathetic ear when I was upset.
words.example_complex: Whenever the team faced problems, the manager was known for lending a sympathetic ear before offering any advice.

words.vi_meaning: buổi hẹn hò giữa hai người chưa từng gặp nhau trước đó
words.definition_en: a romantic meeting between two people who have never met before
collocations: set sb up on a blind date
words.example_simple: My friend arranged a blind date for me.
words.example_complex: Although she was nervous about going on a blind date, the evening turned out surprisingly well and they are now engaged.
words.false_friend_note: 'Blind' here means the people haven't met, not that anyone cannot see.

words.vi_meaning: cố tình gây sự, kiếm chuyện cãi nhau với ai
words.definition_en: to deliberately start an argument with someone
words.example_simple: He picked a quarrel with his neighbour over the fence.
words.example_complex: Tired and irritable after the long journey, he seemed determined to pick a quarrel with everyone around him.
words.false_friend_note: 'Pick' here means 'deliberately start', not 'choose' or 'gather'.

words.vi_meaning: cực kỳ xinh đẹp, đẹp tuyệt trần
words.definition_en: extremely beautiful or attractive
words.example_simple: She looked absolutely gorgeous in her wedding dress.
words.example_complex: The bride looked absolutely gorgeous as she walked down the aisle, and the whole room fell silent in admiration.

words.vi_meaning: làn da khỏe khoắn, rạng rỡ, tràn đầy sức sống
words.definition_en: skin that looks healthy, glowing and full of energy
words.example_simple: Drinking water gives you a radiant complexion.
words.example_complex: After a week of proper sleep and a good diet, she had a radiant complexion that made her look years younger.
words.false_friend_note: 'Complexion' refers to the skin of the face, not one's temperament or 'complex'.

words.vi_meaning: thân hình đồng hồ cát (eo thon, ngực và hông nở cân đối)
words.definition_en: a woman's body shape with a narrow waist and fuller bust and hips
words.example_simple: The dress showed off her hourglass figure.
words.example_complex: Vintage fashion of the 1950s was designed to emphasise an hourglass figure, with fitted waists and full skirts.

words.vi_meaning: trông cực kỳ giống (ai/cái gì đó)
words.definition_en: to look very similar to someone or something
collocations: bear a striking resemblance to sb
words.example_simple: He bears a striking resemblance to his father.
words.example_complex: The young actress bears a striking resemblance to the famous star she plays, which made her perfect for the role.
words.false_friend_note: 'Bear' here means 'to have/carry', not the animal.

words.vi_meaning: xấu xí kinh khủng, xấu đến ghê rợn
words.definition_en: extremely ugly in a shocking or unpleasant way
words.example_simple: The mask was hideously ugly.
words.example_complex: The building was so hideously ugly that residents campaigned for years to have it torn down.

words.vi_meaning: lông mày rậm, lông mày dày
words.definition_en: thick eyebrows with a lot of hair
words.example_simple: The old man had bushy eyebrows.
words.example_complex: His bushy eyebrows drew together in a frown whenever he was concentrating hard on a difficult problem.

words.vi_meaning: ria mép dày, bộ ria rậm
words.definition_en: a lot of thick hair growing above a man's upper lip.
words.example_simple: My grandfather has a thick mustache.
words.example_complex: With his thick mustache and round glasses, he looked exactly like the professor in the old photograph.

words.vi_meaning: râu rậm xồm xoàm; lông trên mặt (râu ria nói chung)
words.definition_en: a long, untidy beard; 'facial hair' means any hair on the face such as a beard or mustache.
words.example_simple: He grew a shaggy beard over the winter.
words.example_complex: After months in the mountains without a razor, he came home with a shaggy beard and far more facial hair than his wife remembered.

words.vi_meaning: thân hình săn chắc, vóc dáng thể thao
words.definition_en: a fit, strong and well-proportioned body, like that of a sportsperson.
words.example_simple: The swimmer has an athletic build.
words.example_complex: Years of training had given her an athletic build that made climbing the steep trail look effortless.

words.definition_en: round, slightly fat cheeks, often seen as cute on children.
words.example_simple: The baby has chubby cheeks.
words.example_complex: Everyone wanted to pinch the toddler's chubby cheeks as he giggled at the party.

words.vi_meaning: có ngoại hình nổi bật, gây ấn tượng mạnh
words.definition_en: to look very noticeable, attractive or impressive in a way that gets attention.
words.example_simple: She has a striking appearance.
words.example_complex: With her silver hair and bright green eyes, the actress had such a striking appearance that people turned to look as she passed.

words.vi_meaning: mũi thẳng; mũi hếch (đầu mũi hơi hướng lên)
words.definition_en: a nose with a straight line; an 'upturned nose' curves slightly up at the tip.
words.example_simple: She has a small upturned nose.
words.example_complex: The portrait showed a man with a perfectly straight nose, while his daughter beside him had a playful upturned nose.
words.false_friend_note: 'Upturned' means turned up, not 'unturned'; it does not mean the nose is upside down.

words.definition_en: wide, strong shoulders; also used figuratively for someone able to handle responsibility.
words.example_simple: The rugby player has broad shoulders.
words.example_complex: His broad shoulders filled the doorway, but everyone knew he was gentle and kind.

words.vi_meaning: cánh tay cơ bắp, cánh tay vạm vỡ
words.definition_en: arms with well-developed, strong muscles.
words.example_simple: The boxer has muscular arms.
words.example_complex: He lifted the heavy boxes with ease, his muscular arms showing the results of years at the gym.

words.vi_meaning: một quý ông đẫy đà (hơi mập, đường bệ)
words.definition_en: a rather fat, dignified-looking man, usually older.
words.example_simple: A portly gentleman sat in the corner.
words.example_complex: The portly gentleman in the velvet waistcoat raised his glass and gave a long, cheerful speech.
words.false_friend_note: 'Portly' is a polite word for rather fat; it is not related to 'port' (a harbour).

words.vi_meaning: phẳng lì, bẹp dí (rất phẳng, không nhô lên chút nào)
words.definition_en: completely flat, with no bumps or curves at all.
collocations: the land is flat as a pancake
words.example_simple: The countryside here is as flat as a pancake.
words.example_complex: After the tyre burst, it was as flat as a pancake, and we had to push the car to the nearest garage.
words.false_friend_note: The idiom describes flatness, not thinness; the seed 'gầy đét' (very thin) is a different sense.

words.word: as white as a sheet / ghost
words.vi_meaning: trắng bệch, mặt cắt không còn giọt máu (vì sợ hãi hoặc ốm)
words.definition_en: very pale in the face, usually because of fear, shock or illness.
collocations: go as white as a sheet
turn as white as a ghost
words.example_simple: She went as white as a sheet when she heard the news.
words.example_complex: The moment the doctor mentioned surgery, his face turned as white as a ghost and he had to sit down.

words.vi_meaning: bầm tím (đầy vết bầm do bị đánh hoặc va đập)
words.definition_en: covered in bruises from being hit or after a fall.
words.example_simple: He fell off his bike and was black and blue.
words.example_complex: After the rough rugby match, his legs were black and blue, but he was still grinning about the win.

words.word: long in the tooth (to do sth)
words.vi_meaning: quá già để làm một việc gì đó
words.definition_en: rather old, and perhaps too old for a particular activity.
collocations: a bit long in the tooth
too long in the tooth for
words.example_simple: I'm a bit long in the tooth for late-night parties.
words.example_complex: He joked that he was getting too long in the tooth to keep playing football with men half his age.

words.vi_meaning: chỉ người đã đứng tuổi nhưng cố ăn mặc trẻ trung (cưa sừng làm nghé)
words.definition_en: an older woman who dresses in a style meant for someone much younger.
collocations: look like mutton dressed as lamb
a case of mutton dressed as lamb
dress like mutton dressed as lamb
words.example_simple: Some people said she looked like mutton dressed as lamb.
words.example_complex: The critics unkindly called the middle-aged singer mutton dressed as lamb, though her fans loved her bold, youthful outfits.
words.false_friend_note: This idiom is usually used about women and is critical, so use it carefully as it can be rude.

words.vi_meaning: không còn trẻ nữa, đã có tuổi
words.definition_en: no longer young; used, often humorously, about someone getting old.
words.example_simple: He's no spring chicken, but he still runs every day.
words.example_complex: I may be no spring chicken these days, but I can still dance all night when the right song comes on.

words.vi_meaning: đã qua thời đỉnh cao, già rồi (không còn giỏi/minh mẫn như trước)
words.definition_en: old and no longer as able, useful or attractive as before.
words.example_simple: He thinks he's over the hill at fifty.
words.example_complex: The champion refused to believe he was over the hill and trained harder than ever for one final match.

words.word: as different as chalk and cheese
words.vi_meaning: hoàn toàn khác nhau, khác nhau một trời một vực
words.definition_en: two people or things that are completely different from each other.
collocations: as different as chalk and cheese
words.example_simple: The two brothers are as different as chalk and cheese.
words.example_complex: Although they had grown up in the same house, the sisters were as different as chalk and cheese in everything from taste to temperament.

words.vi_meaning: khỏe như vâm, rất khỏe mạnh
words.definition_en: very healthy and in very good physical condition.
words.example_simple: My grandmother is ninety but as fit as a fiddle.
words.example_complex: After six months of swimming and eating well, he felt as fit as a fiddle and easily kept up with his teenage sons.
words.false_friend_note: The word 'fiddle' means a violin, but here the phrase simply means healthy, not musical.

words.word: like two peas in a pod
words.vi_meaning: giống nhau như hai giọt nước
words.definition_en: two people who are very similar in looks or behaviour.
collocations: like two peas in a pod
as alike as two peas in a pod
they're two peas in a pod
words.example_simple: The twins are like two peas in a pod.
words.example_complex: In their matching coats and identical smiles, the sisters looked like two peas in a pod as they waved from the platform.

words.definition_en: to fit perfectly, especially clothes or shoes.
collocations: the dress fits like a glove
words.example_simple: These new shoes fit like a glove.
words.example_complex: The tailor had done wonderful work, and the suit fit like a glove when he tried it on for the wedding.

words.vi_meaning: đỏ bừng mặt (vì xấu hổ, ngượng hoặc nóng)
words.definition_en: with a very red face, usually because you are embarrassed, hot, or angry
collocations: turn as red as a beetroot
go as red as a beetroot
words.example_simple: She went as red as a beetroot when the teacher read her poem aloud.
words.example_complex: The moment he realised the whole office had heard his mistake, he turned as red as a beetroot and stared at the floor.

words.vi_meaning: tươi tỉnh, khỏe khoắn và tràn đầy sức sống
words.definition_en: full of energy and looking healthy and rested
collocations: feel as fresh as a daisy
wake up as fresh as a daisy
look as fresh as a daisy
words.example_simple: After a good night's sleep, I felt as fresh as a daisy.
words.example_complex: Despite the overnight flight, she stepped off the plane as fresh as a daisy and headed straight into the meeting.

words.vi_meaning: trêu chọc, chơi khăm ai đó
words.definition_en: to do something to trick or tease someone, usually for fun
words.example_simple: The children played a joke on their teacher on April Fools' Day.
words.example_complex: He thought it would be funny to play a trick on his brother, but the prank went too far and everyone got upset.

words.word: tell/crack a joke; take a joke
words.vi_meaning: kể/nói chuyện đùa; biết chấp nhận bị trêu chọc
words.definition_en: to say something funny to make people laugh; to be able to accept being teased without getting upset
words.example_simple: He cracked a joke and everyone started laughing.
words.example_complex: She loves to tell jokes at parties, but she can't take a joke herself and sulks whenever someone teases her.

words.vi_meaning: nguồn năng lượng vô hạn, tràn đầy sức lực
words.definition_en: a very large amount of energy that seems to have no limit
words.example_simple: Young children seem to have boundless energy.
words.example_complex: With boundless energy and a refusal to quit, she juggled a full-time job, two courses and a young family without ever seeming tired.

words.word: have confidence in somebody / gain somebody's confidence
words.vi_meaning: tin tưởng vào ai; chiếm được lòng tin của ai
words.definition_en: to trust or believe in someone; to make someone trust you
words.example_simple: The team has confidence in their new coach.
words.example_complex: It took months of honest work for the young manager to gain her colleagues' confidence, but once they trusted her, morale improved quickly.
words.false_friend_note: 'Confidence' here means trust in someone, not only the sense 'sự tự tin' (self-assurance).

words.vi_meaning: tính cách vui vẻ, sôi nổi và hoạt bát
words.definition_en: a cheerful, lively and enthusiastic character
words.example_simple: Her bubbly personality makes everyone feel welcome.
words.example_complex: Customers were drawn to the café partly for the coffee but mostly for the owner's bubbly personality, which turned every visit into a chat.

words.vi_meaning: bình tĩnh, điềm tĩnh, không hề nao núng
words.definition_en: very calm and relaxed, especially in a difficult situation
collocations: stay as cool as a cucumber
remain as cool as a cucumber
as cool as a cucumber under pressure
words.example_simple: Even during the exam, he stayed as cool as a cucumber.
words.example_complex: While the rest of the crew panicked, the captain remained as cool as a cucumber and calmly guided the ship back to shore.

words.word: have a tendency to do something
words.vi_meaning: có xu hướng làm gì đó
words.definition_en: to be likely to behave or happen in a particular way
words.example_simple: He has a tendency to arrive late.
words.example_complex: Managers who have a tendency to micromanage often find that their teams become less confident and less productive over time.

words.vi_meaning: đưa ra quyết định vội vàng, tức thời
words.definition_en: to decide something very quickly, often without enough thought
words.example_simple: Don't make a snap decision about such an important thing.
words.example_complex: Under pressure from the crowd, the referee made a snap decision that he would spend the rest of the match regretting.

words.vi_meaning: giữ bí mật, không tiết lộ điều gì
words.definition_en: to not tell anyone about something private or confidential
words.example_simple: Can you keep a secret? I'm getting married.
words.example_complex: She had promised to keep the news a secret, but the temptation to tell her best friend proved almost impossible to resist.

words.vi_meaning: hằn học, oán giận ai; ôm mối ác cảm với ai
words.definition_en: to continue to feel angry or resentful towards someone about something in the past
words.example_simple: She still bears a grudge against her old boss.
words.example_complex: Although the argument had happened years ago, he clearly still bore a grudge against his brother and refused to speak to him at the reunion.

words.vi_meaning: thẳng thắn đến mức phũ phàng, nói thật không nể nang
words.definition_en: telling the truth in a very direct way, even if it hurts someone's feelings
words.example_simple: To be brutally honest, I didn't enjoy the film.
words.example_complex: She valued her mentor precisely because he was brutally honest, telling her exactly what was wrong with her work when everyone else offered polite praise.

words.vi_meaning: nét tính cách ương bướng, cứng đầu
words.definition_en: a part of someone's character that makes them refuse to change their mind
words.example_simple: He has a stubborn streak and never admits he's wrong.
words.example_complex: Beneath her gentle manner ran a stubborn streak, and once she had decided on a plan, no amount of arguing could make her change it.

words.vi_meaning: trí thông minh sắc sảo; nhanh trí, lanh lợi
words.definition_en: the ability to think and make clever, funny remarks very quickly
words.example_simple: Her sharp wit makes her fun to talk to.
words.example_complex: The talk-show host was famous for a sharp wit that could turn an awkward silence into laughter within seconds.

words.vi_meaning: thô lỗ hết sức, cực kỳ khiếm nhã
words.definition_en: extremely and clearly impolite, with no excuse
words.example_simple: It was downright rude of him to ignore her question.
words.example_complex: What started as mild sarcasm quickly became downright rude, and the other guests began to feel embarrassed for the host.

words.vi_meaning: cơn giận bị dồn nén, kìm nén lâu ngày
words.definition_en: strong angry feelings that you have kept inside and not expressed
words.example_simple: He finally let out all his pent-up anger.
words.example_complex: After months of staying silent at work, all her pent-up anger burst out during one small disagreement that had nothing to do with the real problem.

words.vi_meaning: sự thù địch công khai, thái độ chống đối ra mặt
words.definition_en: unfriendly or aggressive feelings that are shown clearly and not hidden
words.example_simple: The plan was met with open hostility from local residents.
words.example_complex: Relations between the two departments had moved from quiet rivalry to open hostility, and meetings often ended in shouting.

words.vi_meaning: tràn đầy năng lượng, hừng hực sức sống
words.definition_en: to be extremely full of energy and enthusiasm
words.example_simple: The puppy was bursting with energy all morning.
words.example_complex: After a two-week holiday, she came back to the office bursting with energy and ideas that transformed the stalled project.

words.vi_meaning: vẻ mặt trống rỗng, thẫn thờ, vô cảm
words.definition_en: a face that shows no emotion, interest or understanding
words.example_simple: She stared at me with a blank expression.
words.example_complex: When the teacher asked the question, she was met with a row of blank expressions that told her no one had done the reading.

words.vi_meaning: tiếp đón ai một cách lạnh nhạt, thờ ơ; tỏ ra lãnh đạm với ai
words.definition_en: to welcome or treat someone in an unfriendly, unenthusiastic way
words.example_simple: The new manager gave me a cool reception on my first day.
words.example_complex: Although the committee had invited him, they gave his proposal such a cool reception that he left the meeting feeling unwelcome.
words.false_friend_note: Here 'cool' means unfriendly/cold, not the slang 'cool' meaning great or impressive.

words.vi_meaning: tính hài hước, khiếu hài hước
words.definition_en: the ability to understand and enjoy things that are funny
words.example_simple: She has a great sense of humour and makes everyone laugh.
words.example_complex: What I admire most about him is his sharp sense of humour, which lets him find something to laugh about even in difficult times.

words.vi_meaning: ý thức trách nhiệm, tinh thần trách nhiệm
words.definition_en: the feeling that you should behave well and take care of your duties
words.example_simple: Owning a pet gives children a sense of responsibility.
words.example_complex: Her strong sense of responsibility meant she stayed late to finish the report rather than leaving it for a colleague.

words.vi_meaning: trí tưởng tượng phong phú, sống động
words.definition_en: a strong ability to form clear and lively pictures or ideas in your mind
words.example_simple: The little boy has a vivid imagination and invents new games every day.
words.example_complex: Thanks to her vivid imagination, she was able to describe places she had never visited as if she had lived there.

words.vi_meaning: đang có tâm trạng tốt / tâm trạng tồi tệ
words.definition_en: to feel happy and cheerful, or unhappy and irritable, at a particular time
collocations: put someone in a good mood
words.example_simple: Dad is in a good mood today, so let's ask him now.
words.example_complex: She had been in a bad mood all morning, so nobody dared to bring up the extra weekend shifts.

words.vi_meaning: đặt ra tiêu chuẩn cao cho ai
words.definition_en: to expect someone to reach a very high level of quality or behaviour
words.example_simple: Our teacher sets high standards for us in every subject.
words.example_complex: Because his parents had always set high standards for him, he felt anxious whenever his results were merely average.

words.vi_meaning: cực kì trung thành, hết mực chung thủy
words.definition_en: extremely faithful and devoted to someone or something
words.example_simple: The dog is fiercely loyal to its owner.
words.example_complex: Even after the scandal, his oldest friends remained fiercely loyal, refusing to say a word against him.

words.vi_meaning: có tính ích kỉ (đôi khi bộc lộ trong tính cách)
words.definition_en: to have a part of your character that is selfish, showing at times
words.example_simple: He is kind, but he does have a selfish streak.
words.example_complex: Despite her generosity in public, those close to her knew she had a selfish streak that surfaced whenever money was involved.
words.false_friend_note: 'Streak' here means a trait in one's character, not a stripe or a run of luck only.

words.vi_meaning: đặt lợi ích của người khác lên trên (bản thân)
words.definition_en: to consider other people's needs as more important than your own
words.example_simple: She always puts others first and helps whenever she can.
words.example_complex: Nurses who consistently put others first can burn out unless they also learn to protect their own wellbeing.

words.vi_meaning: cực kì nhút nhát (đến mức khổ sở, khó xử)
words.definition_en: so shy that it causes you distress in social situations
words.example_simple: He was painfully shy and hated speaking in class.
words.example_complex: As a painfully shy teenager, she would rehearse simple phone calls for minutes before daring to dial.
words.false_friend_note: 'Painfully' here is an intensifier meaning 'extremely', not that it physically hurts.

words.vi_meaning: cực kì tự tin, tự tin tuyệt đối
words.definition_en: extremely and completely sure of yourself and your abilities
words.example_simple: She walked on stage looking supremely confident.
words.example_complex: He gave a supremely confident answer in the interview, yet later admitted he had been terrified inside.

words.vi_meaning: bớt nhút nhát hơn, trở nên cởi mở và tự tin hơn
words.definition_en: to become less shy and more willing to talk to people
collocations: help someone come out of their shell
really come out of one's shell
words.example_simple: After joining the club, she started to come out of her shell.
words.example_complex: The drama teacher had a gift for helping even the quietest students come out of their shells within a few weeks.

words.vi_meaning: có lòng tự trọng thấp/cao; tự ti hoặc tự tin về giá trị bản thân
words.definition_en: to have a low or high opinion of your own worth and abilities
words.example_simple: Constant criticism can give a child low self-esteem.
words.example_complex: Therapists distinguish healthy high self-esteem from a superiority complex, in which someone masks deep insecurity by acting better than everyone else.

words.vi_meaning: có tính chai lì, không dễ bị tổn thương bởi lời chỉ trích
words.definition_en: to be able to ignore criticism or insults and not be upset by them
words.example_simple: You need a thick skin to work in customer service.
words.example_complex: Years of harsh reviews had given the actress a thick skin, so the latest criticism barely fazed her.
words.false_friend_note: This means emotionally resistant to criticism, not literally having thick skin or being unfeeling.

words.vi_meaning: có tính nhát gan, hèn nhát
words.definition_en: to have a tendency to be cowardly
collocations: a yellow streak a mile wide
words.example_simple: He talks tough, but he has a yellow streak.
words.example_complex: When real danger appeared, the yellow streak he had always hidden came out and he ran without helping anyone.
words.false_friend_note: 'Yellow' here idiomatically means cowardly, not the colour or anything to do with jealousy.

words.vi_meaning: hiền lành, hiền như cục đất (dịu dàng, không hung hăng)
words.definition_en: very gentle, calm and harmless in nature
words.example_simple: Despite his size, he is as gentle as a lamb.
words.example_complex: The huge guard dog looked terrifying, but at home it was as gentle as a lamb with the children.
words.false_friend_note: The OCR 'alamp' is 'a lamb'; the simile compares a gentle person to a lamb, not a lamp.

words.vi_meaning: bộc lộ bản chất thật, để lộ bộ mặt thật (thường là xấu)
words.definition_en: to reveal what you are really like, especially when it is unpleasant
synonyms: come out in your true colours
words.example_simple: He showed his true colours when he lied to get the promotion.
words.example_complex: Only when the money ran out did his so-called friends show their true colours and abandon him.
words.false_friend_note: Idiomatic: 'colours' means character/nature here, not paint or literal colours.

words.vi_meaning: rất ngoan ngoãn, cư xử rất tốt (thường nói về trẻ em)
words.definition_en: very well-behaved, obedient and good-natured
collocations: the children were good as gold
words.example_simple: The baby was as good as gold during the flight.
words.example_complex: The teacher was surprised to hear that pupils who were as good as gold in her class caused chaos at home.
words.false_friend_note: This describes good behaviour, not the value or price of gold.

words.vi_meaning: bướng bỉnh, cứng đầu như một con la
words.definition_en: extremely stubborn and unwilling to change your mind
words.example_simple: My grandfather is as stubborn as a mule about using new technology.
words.example_complex: Negotiations dragged on because the chairman was as stubborn as a mule and refused to compromise on a single point.

words.vi_meaning: cứng rắn, lạnh lùng, tàn nhẫn; không dễ mềm lòng
words.definition_en: very tough and showing no sympathy or emotion
words.example_simple: The coach is as hard as nails and never accepts excuses.
words.example_complex: She appeared as hard as nails in the boardroom, yet volunteered every weekend at the shelter.
words.false_friend_note: 'Hard as nails' means emotionally tough/ruthless, not physically hard or difficult.

words.vi_meaning: vui sướng, hài lòng vô cùng; mừng rơn
words.definition_en: extremely pleased, delighted, or satisfied about something
collocations: as pleased as punch about it
words.example_simple: She was as pleased as punch when she passed her driving test.
words.example_complex: When he heard that his short story had won first prize, he was as pleased as punch and couldn't stop grinning all evening.
words.false_friend_note: 'Punch' here is the Punch puppet character, not the drink or a blow with the fist.

words.vi_meaning: phấn khích đến mức khó tin, phấn khích quá mức
words.definition_en: excited to a degree that seems almost silly or over the top
words.example_simple: The kids were ridiculously excited about the trip to the zoo.
words.example_complex: I know it's only a concert, but I've been ridiculously excited about it for weeks and have already planned my whole outfit.

words.vi_meaning: thất vọng cay đắng, vô cùng thất vọng
words.definition_en: very deeply and painfully disappointed about something
words.example_simple: He was bitterly disappointed when he didn't get the job.
words.example_complex: The fans were bitterly disappointed after their team, which had led for most of the match, conceded a goal in the final minute.
words.false_friend_note: 'Bitterly' here means intensely/painfully, not that something tastes bitter.

words.vi_meaning: hạnh phúc ngập tràn, sung sướng tột độ
words.definition_en: perfectly and completely happy, without any worries
words.example_simple: They were blissfully happy on their wedding day.
words.example_complex: For the first few months after moving to the countryside, they felt blissfully happy, far from the noise and stress of the city.

words.vi_meaning: lo lắng đến phát ốm, lo sốt vó
words.definition_en: extremely worried about someone or something
words.example_simple: I was worried sick when you didn't answer your phone.
words.example_complex: His parents were worried sick all night, ringing hospitals and friends, until he finally walked through the door at dawn.
words.false_friend_note: 'Sick' here means intensely, not physically ill or feeling nauseous.

words.vi_meaning: trong tâm trạng u ám, đang cáu kỉnh khó chịu
words.definition_en: feeling very angry, gloomy, or bad-tempered
collocations: put sb in a black mood
in a black mood all day
words.example_simple: Dad has been in a black mood since he lost his keys.
words.example_complex: After the meeting went badly, she was in such a black mood that no one dared to speak to her for the rest of the afternoon.
words.false_friend_note: 'Black' describes the mood as dark/gloomy; it has no connection to skin colour.

words.vi_meaning: sôi sục tức giận, giận sôi máu
words.definition_en: feeling extremely angry but often not showing it openly
words.example_simple: She was seething with anger after he broke his promise.
words.example_complex: He said nothing, but inside he was seething with anger at the way his ideas had been dismissed in front of everyone.

words.vi_meaning: thành thật xin lỗi, rất lấy làm tiếc
words.definition_en: very sorry; used to apologise politely and sincerely
words.example_simple: I'm terribly sorry, I didn't mean to step on your foot.
words.example_complex: We are terribly sorry for the delay to your order, and we'd like to offer you a discount on your next purchase to make up for it.
words.false_friend_note: 'Terribly' here just means 'very'; it does not mean something terrible happened.

words.vi_meaning: người suy sụp tinh thần, người rối loạn cảm xúc
words.definition_en: someone who is extremely upset and unable to cope emotionally
words.example_simple: After the funeral she was an emotional wreck.
words.example_complex: By the end of the exam season he had become an emotional wreck, barely sleeping and bursting into tears over the smallest things.
words.false_friend_note: 'Wreck' here means a person in a bad state, not a shipwreck or crashed vehicle.

words.vi_meaning: ngạc nhiên một cách thú vị, bất ngờ một cách dễ chịu
words.definition_en: surprised in a good way because something was better than expected
words.example_simple: I was pleasantly surprised by how tasty the cheap meal was.
words.example_complex: Having expected a dull evening, we were pleasantly surprised to discover that the small theatre was putting on a genuinely brilliant show.

words.vi_meaning: vô cùng biết ơn, biết ơn sâu sắc
words.definition_en: extremely thankful to someone for something
words.example_simple: I'm immensely grateful for all your help.
words.example_complex: The family said they were immensely grateful to the neighbours who had rushed in to rescue them from the burning house.

words.vi_meaning: ngập tràn cảm xúc, xúc động đến nghẹn ngào
words.definition_en: feeling such strong emotions that you can hardly control yourself
words.example_simple: She was overwhelmed with emotion when she saw her old friend.
words.example_complex: As the crowd rose to applaud, the retiring teacher was so overwhelmed with emotion that she struggled to finish her speech.

words.vi_meaning: buồn thảm, buồn đến tuyệt vọng
words.definition_en: extremely and hopelessly sad
words.example_simple: She felt desperately sad after her cat died.
words.example_complex: It is a desperately sad film about a family torn apart by war, and I found myself in tears long before the end.

words.vi_meaning: làm ai đó thất vọng, phụ lòng ai
words.definition_en: to disappoint someone by failing to do what they expected of you
words.example_simple: You promised to help, so please don't let me down.
words.example_complex: He felt he had let his parents down by dropping out of university, even though they told him they only wanted him to be happy.
words.false_friend_note: This means to disappoint, not literally to lower someone down.

words.vi_meaning: một cú sốc khó chịu, một phen hoảng hồn
words.definition_en: a sudden unpleasant surprise that upsets you
words.example_simple: I got a nasty shock when I saw the huge phone bill.
words.example_complex: Opening the fridge to find it completely empty gave her a nasty shock, and she realised she had forgotten to do the weekly shopping.
words.false_friend_note: 'Shock' here is an emotional jolt, not an electric shock.

words.vi_meaning: ghen tị, đỏ mắt vì ganh tị
words.definition_en: very jealous of what someone else has or has achieved
words.example_simple: When she showed off her new car, I was green with envy.
words.example_complex: His colleagues were green with envy when he came back from his promotion interview with an office overlooking the whole city.
words.false_friend_note: 'Green' here means jealous; it does not refer to being inexperienced or feeling ill.

words.word: rub someone up the wrong way
words.vi_meaning: chọc tức ai đó, làm ai đó khó chịu bực mình
words.definition_en: to annoy or irritate someone, often without meaning to
collocations: rub sb up the wrong way
really rub sb up the wrong way
seem to rub sb up the wrong way
words.example_simple: His rude jokes rubbed everyone up the wrong way.
words.example_complex: She's very capable, but her blunt manner tends to rub new colleagues up the wrong way before they get to know her.
words.false_friend_note: In American English the usual form is 'rub someone the wrong way' (without 'up').

words.vi_meaning: một chút ghen tị, hơi ganh tị
words.definition_en: a small amount of jealousy or envy
collocations: a bit of jealousy between them
words.example_simple: There was a bit of jealousy when my sister got a bigger room.
words.example_complex: A bit of jealousy is normal in any relationship, but if it starts controlling how you behave, it can become a real problem.

words.word: not on speaking terms with sb
words.vi_meaning: bất hòa đến mức không nói chuyện với ai; giận nhau không thèm nói
words.definition_en: so angry with someone that you refuse to talk to them
collocations: not on speaking terms with sb
words.example_simple: The two brothers haven't been on speaking terms for years.
words.example_complex: After the argument over their father's will, the sisters were not on speaking terms with each other and communicated only through their lawyers.

words.word: be afraid of your own shadow
words.vi_meaning: nhát như cáy, sợ bóng sợ gió; quá nhút nhát rụt rè
words.definition_en: to be very nervous or easily frightened, even without real danger
collocations: be afraid of your own shadow
words.example_simple: He's so nervous he's afraid of his own shadow.
words.example_complex: Living alone in the big old house for the first time, she became afraid of her own shadow, jumping at every creak and gust of wind.

words.vi_meaning: làm cho ai đó phát điên, chọc tức ai đó đến mức khó chịu
words.definition_en: to make someone very annoyed or irritated
collocations: really drive me up the wall
the noise drives her up the wall
kids drive parents up the wall
words.example_simple: My little brother drives me up the wall when he keeps asking questions.
words.example_complex: The constant hum of the broken air conditioner, combined with the neighbour's late-night music, was slowly driving her up the wall.

words.vi_meaning: đau buồn tột độ, tang thương, ưu phiền
words.definition_en: feeling extremely sad, especially because someone has died
words.example_simple: The grief-stricken mother could not stop crying at the funeral.
words.example_complex: Grief-stricken and unable to speak, the survivors stood silently as the names of the victims were read aloud.

words.vi_meaning: do (ai đó) gây ra, dưới tay ai (thường là điều xấu)
words.definition_en: caused by or received from a particular person, usually something bad
words.example_simple: Many people suffered at the hands of the cruel king.
words.example_complex: The team endured a humiliating defeat at the hands of a side they had beaten easily only a month before.

words.vi_meaning: đe dọa, gây nguy hiểm cho, tạo ra mối đe dọa đối với
words.definition_en: to be a possible danger to someone or something
words.example_simple: Pollution poses a threat to our health.
words.example_complex: Scientists warn that rising sea levels pose a serious threat to coastal cities around the world.

words.definition_en: a breath that shows you are glad something worrying has ended
collocations: let out a sigh of relief
words.example_simple: She gave a sigh of relief when she saw her lost dog was safe.
words.example_complex: When the final results confirmed that no one had been hurt in the accident, the whole town breathed a collective sigh of relief.
words.false_friend_note: OCR shows 'Sign of relief', but the correct idiom is 'sigh of relief' (a breath), not 'sign'.

words.vi_meaning: trạng thái phấn chấn, sung sướng ngất ngây
words.definition_en: a feeling of very great happiness and excitement
words.example_simple: After winning the prize, she was in a state of euphoria for days.
words.example_complex: The team's last-minute goal sent the entire stadium into a state of euphoria that lasted long after the final whistle.

words.vi_meaning: cảm giác sống có mục đích, có định hướng rõ ràng
words.definition_en: the feeling that your life or actions have meaning and direction
words.example_simple: Volunteering gave her a real sense of purpose.
words.example_complex: After retiring, he struggled to find a sense of purpose until he began mentoring young people in his community.

words.vi_meaning: cảm giác thành công, cảm giác đạt được thành tựu
words.definition_en: the satisfied feeling you get when you have done something difficult
words.example_simple: Finishing the race gave me a great sense of achievement.
words.example_complex: The immense sense of achievement she felt on graduating made all the sleepless nights of study seem worthwhile.

words.vi_meaning: tim đập rộn ràng vì vui mừng hay phấn khích đột ngột
words.definition_en: to suddenly feel a rush of happiness or excitement
words.example_simple: My heart leapt when I saw my name on the list.
words.example_complex: Her heart leapt with joy when, after months of silence, she finally recognised her son's handwriting on the envelope.
words.false_friend_note: This idiom means sudden joy or excitement, not fear; the seed 'sợ hết hồn' (fright) is incorrect.

words.vi_meaning: giấc mơ trở thành hiện thực, ước mơ thành sự thật
words.definition_en: something you have wanted very much that finally happens
words.example_simple: Meeting my favourite singer was a dream come true.
words.example_complex: Owning a small bookshop by the sea had always seemed impossible, so opening the doors on the first morning felt like a dream come true.

words.vi_meaning: hết lời ca ngợi, tỏ ra vui sướng đê mê về điều gì
words.definition_en: to express great enthusiasm and pleasure about something
words.example_simple: She went into raptures over the beautiful garden.
words.example_complex: The critics went into raptures about the young pianist's performance, calling it the finest debut in a generation.

words.vi_meaning: nhảy cẫng lên vì vui sướng
words.definition_en: to be extremely happy and excited about something
words.example_simple: The children jumped for joy when it started to snow.
words.example_complex: When she read that she had passed the exam with the highest mark in her class, she nearly jumped for joy in the middle of the library.

words.vi_meaning: hoàn toàn do may mắn, may mắn thuần túy
words.definition_en: good fortune with no skill or planning involved
words.example_simple: By pure luck, I found my keys under the sofa.
words.example_complex: The scientists insisted the discovery was the result of careful research, but their rivals dismissed it as pure luck.

words.vi_meaning: lạc quan một cách thận trọng, hy vọng nhưng vẫn dè chừng
words.definition_en: hopeful about a situation while still aware it could go wrong
words.example_simple: Doctors are cautiously optimistic about her recovery.
words.example_complex: Economists remain cautiously optimistic about growth next year, though they warn that rising costs could still undermine any recovery.

words.vi_meaning: rất thích thú, lấy làm khoái chí khi làm điều gì
words.definition_en: to get a lot of pleasure from doing something
words.example_simple: He takes great delight in cooking for his friends.
words.example_complex: My grandmother took great delight in reminding us, at every family gathering, of the mischief we had got up to as children.

words.vi_meaning: sự cảm phục, khâm phục sâu sắc
words.definition_en: a very deep feeling of respect and approval for someone
words.example_simple: I have profound admiration for my teachers.
words.example_complex: In his memoir, he expressed profound admiration for the nurses whose quiet courage he had witnessed during the war.

words.vi_meaning: rất thích thú, cảm thấy vui sướng khi làm điều gì
words.definition_en: to enjoy doing something very much
words.example_simple: She takes great pleasure in gardening every morning.
words.example_complex: Even in his eighties, he still found great pleasure in solving the crossword puzzle over breakfast with his wife.

words.vi_meaning: buồn chán, chán nản, tâm trạng ủ rũ
words.definition_en: feeling sad or depressed
collocations: a bit down in the dumps
words.example_simple: He's been down in the dumps since he lost his job.
words.example_complex: After weeks of grey weather and constant bad news, the whole office seemed down in the dumps and nothing could lift the mood.

words.vi_meaning: đồ ăn vặt, thức ăn nhanh không tốt cho sức khỏe
words.definition_en: food that is unhealthy but quick and easy to eat
